title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative:
The Government of Jamaica through the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MLSS) has operationalized a comprehensive, revised national action plan (NAP) on Child Labour (CL). For NAP Strategic Objective 1- Institutional Strengthening, the technical knowledge and capacity for developing tactical recommendations to address CL, of representatives on the inter-ministerial and multi-sectoral National Steering Committee on Child Labour (NASTOCL) has improved, and contributed to partners' inclusion of measures to combat CL risk/ vulnerability factors in individual agency planning processes.
Using the additional national capacity for CL data collection and analysis (resulting from the training of local statisticians in 2019), the ILO-UN Economic Comission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) Child Labour Risk Identification Model (CLRISK) was adapted for Jamaica using the 2016 Jamaica Youth Activity Survey and 2011 Population and Housing Census. Responding to NAP Strategic Objective 6 - Research Capacity, 1 national and 3 county-level risk maps were generated, providing representatives of the multi-sectoral National Steering Committee on Child Labour (NASTOCL) with a visual analysis of the levels of risk of CL in geographical areas and description of the most prevalent risk factors, including sex/gender. Further adaptation of the CLRISK created maps and CL risk profiles at Parish and Constituency level, augmenting the empirical materials available to support NASTOCL members in developing gender-responsive and operational plans at territorial level. The MLSS developed estimates for the implementation of NAP, and submitted them to Cabinet for consideration for funding of CL elimination programmes/ interventions. With the support of the United States, the ILO has supported the MLSS and NASTOCL in the operationalisation of a NAP through technical meetings with NASTOCL members, and by providing technical expertise for the review of the adaptations of the CLRISK statistical model that allow to drill down to the level of constituencies and for the analysis of the results and development of geographic profiles/maps. ILO has also facilitated engagements to validate the deliverables and supported the coordination and execution of virtual national planning workshops using the CLRISK maps, involving the members of NASTOCL. ILO also organised/hosted two intra-Caribbean South-South Cooperation knowledge exchanges on CL issues between Jamaica and other Caribbean Member States (Trinidad and Tobago and Barbados), allowing for sharing of good practices and lessons learned in development of Hazardous Child Labour Lists and approaches to national planning and institutional collaboration.
